feature_under_test: joint loss and recovery of the real-Chrome execution daemon and its separate Artifact provider

environment.mysql: ephemeral MySQL 8.4 with separate non-root migration and runtime accounts
processes: execution daemon process group launching real Chrome

fault_cut.browser_state_before_cut: Attempt running, no Artifact persisted, and controlled origin accepted exactly one document request
fault_cut.cut: SIGKILL both the execution daemon process group that owns Chrome and the separate File provider daemon
fault_cut.recovery_trigger: device disappearance and incarnation fencing allowed the control Actor to expire and redispatch before the 30-second stale TTL

invariants: the two killed daemons are different authenticated devices and OS process groups
both process groups are confirmed stopped before the control plane observes the old Attempt as expired
the Atoll Server and Recruiting control Actor stay online and require no manual database mutation
the expired Attempt produces no accepted Artifact or BackfillOutput and releases its Permit
the originating dispatch is durably settled and attempt_recovered creates a fresh dispatch identity
both devices reconnect with their original identities and the Executor receives a new incarnation
the fresh Attempt persists exactly one DOM response, one effect trace and one BackfillOutput
after Atoll Server restart both devices reconnect and both DOM and trace Resources remain readable

implementation.recovery_mechanism: existing presence/incarnation fence, Attempt recovery, persisted source dispatch, attempt_recovered dispatch, and idempotent Artifact/result contracts

non_claims: remote cloud or object-storage provider behavior
simultaneous Atoll Server or MySQL failure
third-party JavaScript, authentication, anti-bot or availability behavior
Browser throughput or long-window production SLO

acceptance.gate: P9 joint real-Chrome execution daemon and separate local File provider process outage
